messages.subject: Disagreement between empirical.table and empirical.plot ?
parts:
Hi Phil,

I am trying to understand why some items are misfitting the model and how bad this misfit is. In an attempt to compare the observed and the modeled probabilities for one item, I found some disagreements (?) that I do not understand. The attached png shows the results for the empirical.table and empirical.plot from itemplot. As I interpret it, there should be no observations on category 2 for theta >0.22? In fact, in higher thetas, nearly everyone responded category 1, but this is not reflected in the plot.

1) Do the empirical plots not show observed probabilties per decile (dots) on top of the modeled probabilties (curves)?
2) Why do they not show the same results?

Best,
Rico

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Disagreement between empirical.table and empirical.plot ?
parts:
I see what you are saying. The numbers are correct, but the row labels in this case for each element in the list may be incorrect. The last 3 list elements, for example, should probably have row labels c(1,2) rather than c(0,1). We can see that because the leftmost plot has proportions a 0 for each of these slots. If you can provide a brief reproducible example of this then I could try to patch it in the next release. Cheers.

Phil

On Thu, Feb 15, 2018 at 11:59 AM, <rico...@gmail.com> wrote:
Great, a simple solution. I had a feeling it was just me being dense ^^. Here is the code I used below with some sample data (which shows the same problem; table 2 categories while figure has 3):

fit <- mirt(data=data,model=1,itemtype = "graded", SE=T, calcNull = T)
itemfit(x=fit,empirical.plot=1)
itemfit(x=fit,empirical.table=1)


Thank you,
Rico
